messages:
lina_support: FYI, AcmeProd reported a spike and saw ~1200 504s over 12m, customer says API calls hung then failed. raising to incidents.
devon: thanks Lina — any useful traces or a request id we can start from?
samir: saw the alerts, looks like gateway timeout with backend 5xx while pods were starting. quick glance at scale metrics shows HPA didn't kick for ~30s after the metric spike.
neha: I pulled kube events for the tenant's pool: HPA scaled to 0 -> 2 but kube-controller waited due to scaleDownQuiesce window. that quiesce may have suppressed scale-up when bursts are very short.
lina_support: customer repro steps: rapid 200 RPS burst for 20s, then steady 20 RPS. They said any request during burst got 504.
ops_lead: interesting — quiesce is intended to avoid flappy scaleups but here it blocked the initial warmstart. what's the HPA/Cooldown config on that pool?
samir: HPA annotations:
```
autoscaling.kubernetes.io/cooldown: "45s"
redwood.dev/quiesce-window: "60s"
keda.scaleDownCooldown: "30s"
```
so multiple cooldown-ish knobs stacked.
devon: so combined effect = delayed provision while KEDA scaler metric already decayed? that could explain the ~30s lag.
neha: also saw readiness probe timeouts on new pods because model init took ~18s (cold model load + quantized weight fetch). requests hit the gateway in that window.
autoscale-bot: [auto] alert: pool-acme-prod scaled from 0 -> 3 at 5207654390; avg model-init 18.6s; queue length peaked at 410
lina_support: customer also reported intermittent auth 401s mixed in — probably because proxy retries collided with token refresh limit and triggered auth-billing checks. can we isolate?
samir: auth 401s correlate with retry storms from clients when initial request timed out. once they retried with new token it passed, but gateway logged 401s during the window.
ops_lead: immediate mitigation: increase min-replicas on that tenant pool to 1 and add a short warmstart pre-warm policy for bursty tenants. can we patch quickly?
neha: I can roll a config change to set minReplicas=1 + reduce quiesce window to 10s for the tenant pool. patching k8s annotations now. also logging improvement: add a per-request pre-warm tag so we can map requests to a pending warmstart.
devon: please also add a temporary routing fallback to a lighter model variant for that tenant to keep tail latency low during warmstarts.
autoscale-bot: action taken: applied minReplicas=1 for pool-acme-prod at 5207654442
lina_support: customer updated: saw drop in 504s after ~40s, still some residual errors but much better. they asked for repro steps to be shared.
samir: repro notes (for postmortem):
1) simulate 200RPS burst for 20s against a pool with minReplicas=0
2) ensure model size ~6GB cold-load (18s init)
3) HPA quiesce/cooldown stacked values > scale reaction window
4) observe gateway timeout ~15-30s for early requests
commands:
```
# burst load
hey -z 20s -q 200 -c 50 https://api.redwood/test-endpoint
# check events
kubectl -n tenant-acme get hpa,pods -w
```
neha: next steps: short term: keep minReplicas=1 for this tenant, reduce quiesce to 10s, add pre-warm hook. medium: change default quiesce to 10s for bursty profiles and add model-init histogram to console dashboard.
ops_lead: assign postmortem to samir + neha, include runbook update for burst profiles and a playbook to set warmstart on tenants with sprint patterns. also include billing/auth interaction note.
lina_support: I'll follow up with customer and attach reproduction steps + ETA for permanent fix. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
devon: will add canary for fallback routing policy and monitor 5xx rate for next 24h.
samir: creating incident doc and linking metrics/graphs to the ticket. will include sample traces showing the quiesce-threshold race.
